newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian union threatens action against RBA.
newsitem.headline: Australian union threatens action against RBA.

text.p: Australia's Transport Workers Union (TWU) is threatening the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) with industrial action unless the central bank comes up with a good explanation for opposing recent pay claims, media reported on Tuesday.

"If they (the RBA) don't talk to us within 14 days we will conduct rolling industrial action which will mean that if and when we find out that the governor or the deputy governor ever get onto a plane, we will hold stop-work meetings of our membership at the particular airport," TWU federal president Steve Hutchins told the Australian Financial Review newspaper.
Hutchins said TWU members would not guarantee Reserve bank deliveries of cash and coins.
TWU officials were not immediately available and the central bank declined comment.
Last week, the union lost its case for an 11 percent rise in wage rates for about 35,000 truck drivers when the claim was rejected in the Australian Industrial Relations Commission.

The TWU believes public opposition to the pay hike by the Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane and his deputy Stephen Grenville strongly influenced the labour court's decision to reject the claim, the newspaper said.
The Reseve Bank has an inflation target of 2-3 percent, a level depending on wages growth of less than 4.5 percent.
